The PSP Go of 2009 dropped the UMD drive and sold games only as downloads.
Remote Play let it stream and control a PlayStation 3 over Wi-Fi.
Early games were capped at 222 MHz; Sony later let developers use the processor's full 333 MHz.

Its widescreen is 4.3 inches, at 480 × 272 pixels.
It saves to Memory Stick Duo cards.
Its two processors are based on the MIPS R4000.
Slimmer models came in 2007 and 2008, and a budget PSP Street in 2011.
